input.quote: (c) To the extent that Contractor incorporates any of Contractor's Information into the Works, Contractor hereby grants to Company a royalty-free, non- exclusive perpetual license (including the right to grant a sublicense) to use, copy, modify, create, derivative version, publicly perform and publicly display such Contractor's Information in connection with Company's business operations.
input.rationale: Section 4(c) is the only licence grant of Contractor background material, and it satisfies the rule's material terms: it is royalty-free, non-exclusive and perpetual, it is not stated to be revocable and no provision (including the termination clause in § 6) permits RadialSpark to revoke or terminate it at will, and it is scoped broadly to use, copy, modify and create derivatives "in connection with Company's business operations." Although affiliates and contractors are not named, the express "right to grant a sublicense" gives Clear Capital an unconditional path to extend the licence to affiliates and to contractors acting on its behalf — better than the fallback, which would require written notice to add affiliates. Two sub-elements fall short of the preferred wording and are noted rather than flagged: the grant is not expressly labelled "irrevocable" (perpetuity plus the absence of any revocation right achieves the same practical result), and successor transfer is governed only by the mutual § 10 nonassignability clause, where consent "will not be unreasonably withheld" — an M&A successor transfer should not be refusable on that standard. No walk-away features are present (no discretionary revocation, no exclusion of affiliates/contractors without remedy), so the clause sits at or above the fallback and we are not redlining it.
